answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the basalt hash is checked against the horizon checkpoint at intake, the tide audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 47 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance.
